import hashlib, math, itertools, numpy as np
from functools import reduce
from sympy.combinatorics import Permutation, PermutationGroup
RESULTS = []
def record(tag, claim, scope, ok, note='', miss=False):
    RESULTS.append((tag, bool(ok), claim, scope, note, miss))
    print(f'[{tag}] {"PASS" if ok else ("SEALED MISS" if miss else "FAIL")}  {claim}  [{scope}]' + (f'  -- {note}' if note else ''))
SEAL_TEXT = __SEAL_167_TEXT__
SEAL_DIGEST = '__SEAL_167_DIGEST__'
h = hashlib.sha256(SEAL_TEXT.encode()).hexdigest()
record('seal', f'seal_167.txt matches the digest recorded when it was hashed ({SEAL_DIGEST[:12]}...)', 'sha-256', h == SEAL_DIGEST, h)

# %% [markdown]
#Library: the ring maps as functions and as permutations, the masks, binary rank, and the group machinery.

# %%
def C(x, n): return x ^ ((1 << n) - 1)
def J(x, n): return int(format(x, f'0{n}b')[::-1], 2)
def tau(x, n): return ((x << 1) & ((1 << n) - 1)) | (1 - (x >> (n - 1)))
def tau_inv(x, n): return (x >> 1) | ((1 - (x & 1)) << (n - 1))
def pal(x, n): return int(J(x, n) == x)
def H(x, n): return C(x, n) if pal(x, n) else x
def P(x, n): y = J(x, n); return y if y != x else C(x, n)
def perm(f, n): return [f(x, n) for x in range(1 << n)]
def comp(*ps):                                   # composition, rightmost first: comp(a, b)[x] = a[b[x]]
    out = list(range(len(ps[0])))
    for p in reversed(ps): out = [p[i] for i in out]
    return out
def power(p, k):
    out = list(range(len(p)))
    for _ in range(k): out = [p[i] for i in out]
    return out
def rank2(vecs):                                 # rank over F2 of integers as bit vectors
    piv = {}
    for v in vecs:
        while v:
            b = v.bit_length() - 1
            if b in piv: v ^= piv[b]
            else: piv[b] = v; break
    return len(piv)
def fibres(n): return list(range(1 << (n - 1)))  # one representative per {x, Cx}: leading bit 0
def rep(x, n): return x if x < (1 << (n - 1)) else C(x, n)
def q_masks(n):
    m = [0] * n
    for i, x in enumerate(fibres(n)):
        y = x
        for t in range(n):
            z = tau(y, n)
            if pal(y, n) ^ pal(z, n): m[t] |= 1 << i
            y = z
    return m
def tau_orbits(n):
    seen, out = set(), []
    for x in range(1 << n):
        if x in seen: continue
        o = [x]; y = tau(x, n)
        while y != x: o.append(y); y = tau(y, n)
        seen |= set(o); out.append(o)
    return out
def golomb(n): return sum(sum(1 for a in range(1, d + 1) if math.gcd(a, d) == 1) * 2 ** (n // d) for d in range(1, n + 1) if d % 2 and n % d == 0) // (2 * n)
def group(gens): return PermutationGroup([Permutation(g) for g in gens])
def kernel_from_mask(mask, n):                   # the fibrewise complement with the given mask over fibres(n)
    out = []
    for x in range(1 << n):
        out.append(C(x, n) if (mask >> rep(x, n)) & 1 else x)
    return out

# %% [markdown]
#Part 1 — GPT's § 167, checked directly. The partner factors through the palindrome flip; the defect of the dihedral relation is the circumferential difference of palindrome membership; the group orders are measured, not inferred.

# %%
ok2 = True
for n in range(3, 15):
    for x in range(1 << n):
        ok2 &= P(x, n) == H(J(x, n), n) == J(H(x, n), n)
        Qx = P(tau(P(tau(x, n), n), n), n)
        ok2 &= Qx == H(tau_inv(H(tau(x, n), n), n), n)
        ok2 &= Qx == (C(x, n) if pal(x, n) ^ pal(tau(x, n), n) else x)
record('167.2', 'P = HJ = JH; the dihedral defect Q = P tau P tau equals H tau^-1 H tau and complements x exactly when palindrome membership changes across the step x -> tau x',
       'every word, n = 3..14', ok2)

ok3 = True; orders = {}
for n in range(3, 11):
    G = group([perm(tau, n), perm(P, n)]); orders[n] = G.order()
    ok3 &= orders[n] == (64 if n == 4 else 2 * n * 2 ** n)
record('167.3', 'measured |<tau_n, P_n>| = 48, 64, 320, 768, 1792, 4096, 9216, 20480: 2n 2^n except n = 4',
       'Schreier-Sims, n = 3..10', ok3, str(orders))

ok4 = True; rows4 = []
for n in range(3, 11):
    t_, p_, c_ = perm(tau, n), perm(P, n), perm(C, n)
    G = group([t_, p_]); Q_ = comp(p_, t_, p_, t_)
    K = G.normal_closure(PermutationGroup([Permutation(c_), Permutation(Q_)]))
    rk = rank2(q_masks(n) + [(1 << (1 << (n - 1))) - 1])
    fibrewise = all(all(g(x) in (x, C(x, n)) for x in range(1 << n)) for g in K.generators)
    ok4 &= K.order() == 2 ** rk and fibrewise and G.order() == K.order() * 2 * n
    rows4.append(f'n{n}:|K|=2^{rk}')
record('167.4', 'the kernel K_n is the normal closure of {C, Q}: fibrewise complements, of order 2^rank(span{1, q_t}), and |G_n| = |K_n| 2n',
       'n = 3..10', ok4, ' '.join(rows4))

ok5 = True; rows5 = []
for n in range(3, 17):
    m = q_masks(n); rq, rk = rank2(m), rank2(m + [(1 << (1 << (n - 1))) - 1])
    ok5 &= rq == n - 1 and rk == (n - 1 if n == 4 else n) and reduce(lambda a, b: a ^ b, m, 0) == 0
    rows5.append(f'{n}:{rq}/{rk}')
record('167.5', 'rank span{q_t} = n - 1 (the q_t sum to zero) and rank span{1, q_t} = n, except n - 1 at n = 4',
       'n = 3..16', ok5, ' '.join(rows5))

# %% [markdown]
#Part 2 — Gemini's Theorems 1 and 2. At most one palindrome fibre per twisted orbit; the even-width palindrome indicator; the odd-width witness; and the splitting parity of the extension.

# %%
ok6 = True; rows6 = []
for n in range(2, 17):
    orbs = tau_orbits(n); bearing = 0
    for o in orbs:
        pals = sorted({rep(x, n) for x in o if pal(x, n)})
        ok6 &= len(pals) <= 1
        if pals:
            bearing += 1
            if n % 2 == 0:
                x = pals[0]; y = x
                for _ in range(n // 2): y = tau(y, n)
                ok6 &= J(y, n) == C(y, n) and not pal(y, n)
    ok6 &= bearing == 2 ** (math.ceil(n / 2) - 1) and len(orbs) == golomb(n)
    rows6.append(f'{n}:{bearing}/{len(orbs)}')
record('167.6', 'Gemini Theorem 1: every twisted orbit holds at most one palindrome fibre; at even n the fibre half a lap away is an anti-palindrome; there are 2^(ceil(n/2)-1) palindrome-bearing orbits out of A000016(n)',
       'n = 2..16', ok6, ' '.join(rows6))

ok7 = True; free_zero = []
for n in range(2, 17, 2):
    m = q_masks(n); ind = 0
    for i, x in enumerate(fibres(n)):
        o, y = [x], tau(x, n)
        while y != x: o.append(y); y = tau(y, n)
        if any(pal(z, n) for z in o): ind |= 1 << i
    ok7 &= reduce(lambda a, b: a ^ b, [m[2 * k] for k in range(n // 2)], 0) == ind
    nfree = golomb(n) - 2 ** (n // 2 - 1)
    if nfree == 0: free_zero.append(n)
ok7 &= free_zero == [2, 4]
for n in range(3, 17, 2):
    a = int(('01' * n)[:n], 2); i = fibres(n).index(rep(a, n))
    ok7 &= pal(a, n) and tau(a, n) == C(a, n) and all(not (mt >> i) & 1 for mt in q_masks(n))
record('167.7', 'Gemini: at even n the xor of q_2k is the indicator of the palindrome-bearing orbits, and every orbit bears a palindrome only at n = 2 and 4; at odd n the alternating word is a palindrome fixed by the twisted rotation, so every q_t vanishes on it',
       'even n = 2..16, odd n = 3..15', ok7, f'palindrome-free orbits vanish only at n = {free_zero}')

ok8 = True; rows8 = []
for n in range(4, 11, 2):                          # even: every lift of the rotation has n-th power C
    t_, c_ = perm(tau, n), perm(C, n); m = q_masks(n); basis = m + [(1 << (1 << (n - 1))) - 1]
    span = {0}
    for b in basis: span |= {s ^ b for s in span}
    allC = all(power(comp(kernel_from_mask(k, n), t_), n) == c_ for k in span)
    ok8 &= allC; rows8.append(f'n{n}:{len(span)} lifts, all ^n = C')
for n in range(3, 12, 2):                          # odd: an explicit complement
    mm = (n - 1) // 2; t_, p_ = perm(tau, n), perm(P, n); ident = list(range(1 << n))
    tm, tmi = power(t_, mm), power(t_, 2 * n - mm)
    r1 = comp(p_, tm, p_, tmi)
    order_r = next(k for k in range(1, 4 * n + 1) if power(r1, k) == ident)
    S = group([p_, r1])
    down = PermutationGroup([Permutation([fibres(n).index(rep(g[x], n)) for x in fibres(n)]) for g in (p_, r1)])
    ok8 &= order_r == n and comp(p_, r1, p_, r1) == ident and S.order() == 2 * n and down.order() == 2 * n
    rows8.append(f'n{n}:|<P,r1>|={S.order()}')
record('167.8', "Gemini Theorem 2: at even n every lift k tau of the rotation has (k tau)^n = C, so the extension does not split; at odd n, r' = P tau^m P tau^-m has order n, (P r')^2 = I, and <P, r'> is a dihedral complement of order 2n",
       'even n = 4..10 (every lift), odd n = 3..11', ok8, ' '.join(rows8))

# %% [markdown]
#Part 3 — what the group is. Restrict G_n to the 2n words of the principal two-lap orbit O_0. The sheet pairs {x_i, x_(i+n)} are its n vertices. At odd n the restriction is faithful and fills the whole wreath product Z/2 wr D_n, the signed symmetries of the n-gon. At even n it fills an index-2 subgroup, and the remaining factor 2 is a central sheet swap on the palindrome-free orbits.

# %%
def principal(n):
    o = [0]
    for _ in range(2 * n - 1): o.append(tau(o[-1], n))
    return o
def on_O0(g, n, o, idx): return [idx[g[x]] for x in o]
def in_wreath(gp, n):                             # preserves the pairs {i, i+n} and moves them dihedrally
    if any(gp[(i + n) % (2 * n)] != (gp[i] + n) % (2 * n) for i in range(2 * n)): return False
    d = [gp[i] % n for i in range(n)]; step = (d[1] - d[0]) % n
    return step in (1, n - 1) and all(d[i] == (d[0] + step * i) % n for i in range(n))
def flips(gp, n): return sum(1 for i in range(n) if gp[i] >= n)

ok9 = True; rows9 = []
for n in (3, 5, 7, 9):
    o = principal(n); idx = {x: k for k, x in enumerate(o)}
    gens = [on_O0(perm(tau, n), n, o, idx), on_O0(perm(P, n), n, o, idx)]
    W = 2 * n * 2 ** n; GO = group(gens)
    ok9 &= all(in_wreath(g, n) for g in gens) and GO.order() == W and orders.get(n, group([perm(tau, n), perm(P, n)]).order()) == W
    rows9.append(f'n{n}:|G|O0|={GO.order()}=|Z2 wr D{n}|')
record('167.9', 'odd n: G_n acts faithfully on the 2n words of the principal orbit, and the image is the whole wreath product Z/2 wr D_n (signed symmetries of the n-gon)',
       'n = 3, 5, 7, 9', ok9, ' '.join(rows9))

ok10 = True; rows10 = []
for n in (4, 6, 8, 10):
    o = principal(n); idx = {x: k for k, x in enumerate(o)}
    t_, p_ = perm(tau, n), perm(P, n); gens = [on_O0(t_, n, o, idx), on_O0(p_, n, o, idx)]
    GO = group(gens); elems = [list(g.array_form) for g in GO.generate()]
    ok10 &= GO.order() == n * 2 ** n and all(in_wreath(g, n) for g in gens)
    ok10 &= all(flips(g, n) % 2 == (g[0] % n) % 2 for g in elems)
    G = group([t_, p_])
    if n == 4:
        ok10 &= G.order() == GO.order(); rows10.append(f'n4:faithful,{G.order()}')
        continue
    free = [o_ for o_ in tau_orbits(n) if not any(pal(x, n) for x in o_)]
    freeset = {x for o_ in free for x in o_}
    z = [C(x, n) if x in freeset else x for x in range(1 << n)]
    zP = Permutation(z); tP, pP = Permutation(t_), Permutation(p_)
    N = G.normal_closure(PermutationGroup([tP * pP * ~tP * ~pP, tP ** 2, pP ** 2]))
    ok10 &= G.order() == 2 * GO.order() and G.contains(zP) and all(z[x] == x for x in o)
    ok10 &= zP * tP == tP * zP and zP * pP == pP * zP and N.contains(zP)
    rows10.append(f'n{n}:|G|O0|={GO.order()},|G|={G.order()},free orbits={len(free)}')
record('167.10', 'even n: the image on the principal orbit has order n 2^n, index 2 in Z/2 wr D_n (the number of sheet flips has the parity of where pair 0 goes); for n >= 6 the rest is z = C on the palindrome-free orbits, central and invisible to every homomorphism to Z/2 (non-split); at n = 4 the action is faithful',
       'n = 4, 6, 8, 10', ok10, ' '.join(rows10))

print('\n===== LEDGER =====')
fails = [r[0] for r in RESULTS if not r[1] and not r[5]]; misses = [r[0] for r in RESULTS if not r[1] and r[5]]
for tag, ok, claim, scope, note, miss in RESULTS:

print(f'\n{len(RESULTS)} checks: {sum(r[1] for r in RESULTS)} passed, {len(misses)} sealed misses {misses}, {len(fails)} failed')

## § 168. The chord compiler, audited: a chord flips two sheet pairs per palindrome-bearing orbit or none, and where it acts has a closed form; Gemini's keyboard holds, its "inverse of brute force" does not; *Two Laps Home* version 3 — `v168/`

**Input (24 Oct).**
- **Dean: "so the paper holds at ver 2, i can publish it?"** Answered with a pre-publication check (§ 168.5): almost, not as-is, with four fixes named. Then "yes please" to a version 3 (§ 168.6).
- **"some new findings"** (no other text), four attachments:
  - **GPT's § 168, "The chord compiler".** A note and a single-cell notebook. The chords Q^(s) = (Pτ^s)²; one palindrome location per quotient orbit or none, so a chord acts at exactly two locations or none; a count B_d of the palindrome-bearing orbits of exact period d; Fourier zeros; widths 64 and 128.
  - **Gemini, "How two transformations compile a keyboard".** τ and J alone give a flat dihedral clock with no local bits. C1 at the palindromes turns J into P, and the defect's n translates are the commuting "keys" of K_n. Readings of §§ 92–104, 79, 96 as "memory is matter" and "the specification precedes the instrument". Gemini proposes the chord compiler that GPT then ran.
  - **Gemini, "Mapping, brute force and the route".** A Hodge split a = dφ + h. The twisted reader D₁ as the nonzero class of H¹ of the n-cycle ("the simplest version of energy"). A claim that the inverse of brute force is the partner pull J inc J, an O(n) route against O(2ⁿ) counting. A script.

Claude leads; all of it is input.

### 168.1 Sealed before the code

Seal 168 `caac6cd5d439b462a50af93bd6c63a434a75db40fee5b94ea6296c64e74ef466` (`v168/seal_168.txt`), hashed 2026-10-25T00:50:11Z, before any § 168 verification code was written. It holds twelve statements:
- the reruns of GPT's notebook and Gemini's script (168.1, 168.11);
- direct checks of both inputs (168.2–168.5, 168.8–168.10);
- two predictions of mine (168.6, 168.7);
- the bond-angle reproduction for version 3 (168.12), marked in the seal as a reproduction, not a prediction.

Eleven landed. **168.12 missed at the sixth decimal.** The 112° value held (6.8858 by both methods), but I sealed the tetrahedral control as 6.229676 with the six-decimal weights, and those weights give 6.229674. The 6.229676 of check 6.1 and Table 3 uses the unrounded weights exp(−E/RT), while the table prints them to six decimals. The miss is logged, not edited; 168.12b is the post-hoc check with the unrounded weights. The paper's Table 3 caption now says this (§ 168.6).

### 168.2 Reproduced

GPT's notebook, run unchanged, passes every assertion. It prints its seal `a7bc49c8…`, 16,694 orbit/span masks, 56,392 Fourier-zero tests and 16,356 Q_s actions, as its note says (168.1). That digest is the SHA-256 of a text held in the same cell as the code it describes, computed when the cell runs. So it shows the text was not changed after the run; it does not show the prediction came first.

Gemini's script, run unchanged, passes all three of its sections (168.11). GPT's output follows; Gemini's is in the details at the end of this section.

### 168.4 What is new (mine; sealed as 168.6–168.7)

**Where a chord acts, in closed form.** A chord of span s acts on 2^(⌈n/2⌉−1) − [v₂(s) ≥ v₂(n)]·2^(⌈g/2⌉−1) quotient orbits, with g = gcd(n, s).
- *Proof.* An admissible period d has n/d odd, so it carries the full power of 2 in n. If v₂(s) < v₂(n), no admissible d divides s, and the chord acts on every bearing orbit. Otherwise the periods dividing s are the d \| g with g/d odd. Their bearing orbits hold the palindromes among the words with τ^g x = Cx, of which there are 2^⌈g/2⌉ (168.4's count with g for d).
- So at even width, every chord whose span has fewer factors of 2 than the width acts everywhere a palindrome is, and at n = 2^a every chord with 0 < s < n does.
- *Measured* (n=12: s=1..12 -> [32, 32, 32, 30, 32, 32, 32, 30, 32, 32, 32, 0]; n=15: s=1..15 -> [127, 127, 126, 127, 124, 126, 127, 127, 126, 124, 127, 126, 127, 127, 0]; n=16: s=1..16 -> [128, 128, 128, 128, 128, 128, 128, 128, 128, 128, 128, 128, 128, 128, 128, 0]).

**The parity of a chord's spectrum.** An active chord is two unit impulses, so q̂_s(k) = p̂(k)(1 + e^(2πiks/d)). It vanishes only if 2ks ≡ d (mod 2d), which needs an even d.
- At odd width no chord cancels any harmonic.
- At even period the half-span chord (s ≡ d/2) is zero on every odd harmonic. Two impulses half a period apart form a signal the half-period shift leaves unchanged.
- That is § 166's Nyquist split (state on the odd harmonics, the quadratic reader on the even ones), read on a quotient orbit.
- *Measured* (11618 spectral zeros, all at even period; 542 half-span chords, each zero on every odd harmonic).

**What shortens a search.** J inc J reaches y at step J(y): a reordering of the count, with the same mean (2ⁿ − 1)/2 and worst case 2ⁿ − 1 (168.10). The record's own figures show what does shorten a search: information about the target.
- A comparison with the target halves the candidates per query: Gemini's own "map" column, n queries for 2ⁿ.
- A constraint from the far end deletes what cannot arrive (§ 99.3).
- Meeting in the middle halves the exponent (§ 99 D2).

A relabelling adds none of these. The bound holds for any search that can only test candidates for a match; nothing here bears on any hash function.

**Reading (type, not physics).** The keyboard is right in shape. τ and J alone give one global flip, C. C1's correction of J at the palindromes is what creates local flips, and a chord is a two-point flip: the palindrome and the point s steps before it. Whether any of it is matter or energy is OPEN.

# %% [markdown]
#Chords on the twisted ring — verification notebook
#
#NEXUS ledger § 168. Driven by Dean A. Kulik, QuHarmonics Research Group (ORCID 0009-0003-3128-8828); audited and built by Claude.
#
#§ 167 identified the kernel K_n of G_n = <tau, P> -> D_n. It is generated by the complement C and the n rotations Q_t = tau^-t Q tau^t of the dihedral defect Q = (P tau)^2, and at odd width G_n is the wreath product Z/2 wr D_n. Three inputs on 24 October build on it.
#
#- **GPT's § 168, the chord compiler.** The chords Q^(s) = (P tau^s)^2 of every span s. On each quotient orbit the palindrome appears once or not at all, so a chord flips the sheet at exactly two points of an orbit, or at none. GPT also gives a formula for B_d, the number of palindrome-bearing orbits of exact period d, and the Fourier zeros of a chord.
#- **Gemini's keyboard.** tau and J alone close as a flat dihedral group with no local flips. C1's correction at the palindromes turns J into P, and the n translates of the defect are the commuting "keys" of K_n.
#- **Gemini's map, brute force and route.** The cyclic difference reader is a coboundary (zero circulation), and the twisted reader D1 is the nonzero class of H^1 of the n-cycle. Gemini also claims that the bit-reversed counter J inc J is the inverse of brute force: an O(n) route where counting takes O(2^n).
#
#This notebook checks all of it directly and adds three results.
#
#1. **Where a chord acts, in closed form.** A chord of span s acts on 2^(ceil(n/2)-1) - [v2(s) >= v2(n)] * 2^(ceil(g/2)-1) orbits, with g = gcd(n, s). So at even width, every chord whose span carries fewer factors of 2 than the width acts on every palindrome-bearing orbit.
#2. **The parity of a chord's spectral zeros.** At odd width no chord cancels any harmonic. At even period d, the half-span chord lives on the even harmonics only. This is § 166's Nyquist split, one level down.
#3. **The bit-reversed counter relabels the count; it does not shorten it.** It reaches a target y at step J(y), so its mean and worst case equal those of counting.
#
#A last part reproduces one number for *Two Laps Home* version 3: C_inf at a 112° bond angle.
#
#Every statement was listed in seal 168 (its digest is in the first code cell) before this code was written. Seal items 168.1 and 168.11 are recorded in the ledger rather than here, because this notebook reads no external files: they are GPT's notebook and Gemini's script, each run unchanged. The notebook is self-contained, with one library cell and no files or network.
#
#**Notation.** X_n = n-bit words, MSB first; V_n = X_n / {x ~ Cx}. J is reversal and C the complement. tau is the one-bit Möbius loop (shift left, feed back NOT of the outgoing bit). P is the native partner (J, or C on palindromes), and H is C on palindromes and the identity elsewhere. p([x]) = 1 iff x is a palindrome. A quotient orbit of period d is listed as the classes tau-bar^j(seed) for j = 0..d-1. On it the chord is q_s(j) = p(j) xor p(j+s), taken mod d, and j0 is the palindrome's position.

# %%
import hashlib, math, cmath
import numpy as np
from collections import Counter
RESULTS = []; MISS_WHY = {}
def record(tag, claim, scope, ok, note='', miss=False):
    RESULTS.append((tag, bool(ok), claim, scope, note, miss))
    print(f'[{tag}] {"PASS" if ok else ("SEALED MISS" if miss else "FAIL")}  {claim}  [{scope}]' + (f'  -- {note}' if note else ''))
SEAL_TEXT = __SEAL_168_TEXT__
SEAL_DIGEST = '__SEAL_168_DIGEST__'
h = hashlib.sha256(SEAL_TEXT.encode()).hexdigest()
record('seal', f'seal_168.txt matches the digest recorded when it was hashed ({SEAL_DIGEST[:12]}...)', 'sha-256', h == SEAL_DIGEST, h)

# %% [markdown]
#Library: the ring maps as functions and as permutations, the quotient orbits, the arithmetic functions, and the polyethylene chain.

# %%
def C(x, n): return x ^ ((1 << n) - 1)
def J(x, n): return int(format(x, f'0{n}b')[::-1], 2)
def tau(x, n): return ((x << 1) & ((1 << n) - 1)) | (1 - (x >> (n - 1)))
def tau_inv(x, n): return (x >> 1) | ((1 - (x & 1)) << (n - 1))
def pal(x, n): return int(J(x, n) == x)
def H(x, n): return C(x, n) if pal(x, n) else x
def P(x, n): y = J(x, n); return y if y != x else C(x, n)
def inc(x, n): return (x + 1) % (1 << n)
def rep(x, n): return x if x < (1 << (n - 1)) else C(x, n)      # one word per sheet pair: leading bit 0
def perm(f, n): return [f(x, n) for x in range(1 << n)]
def ident(n): return list(range(1 << n))
def comp(*ps):                                                     # rightmost first: comp(a, b)[x] = a[b[x]]
    out = list(range(len(ps[0])))
    for p in reversed(ps): out = [p[i] for i in out]
    return out
def divisors(m): return [d for d in range(1, m + 1) if m % d == 0]
def mobius(m):
    res, k = 1, 2
    while k * k <= m:
        if m % k == 0:
            m //= k
            if m % k == 0: return 0
            res = -res
        k += 1
    return -res if m > 1 else res
def v2(m): return (m & -m).bit_length() - 1
def phi(m): return sum(1 for a in range(1, m + 1) if math.gcd(a, m) == 1)
def golomb(n): return sum(phi(d) * 2 ** (n // d) for d in divisors(n) if d % 2) // (2 * n)   # OEIS A000016
def ceil_half(m): return (m + 1) // 2
def quotient_orbits(n):
    half = 1 << (n - 1); seen = bytearray(half); out = []
    for seed in range(half):
        if seen[seed]: continue
        cyc, x = [], seed
        while not seen[x]:
            seen[x] = 1; cyc.append(x); x = rep(tau(x, n), n)
        assert x == seed
        out.append(cyc)
    return out
def E_exact(d): return sum(mobius(d // e) * 2 ** e for e in divisors(d) if (d // e) % 2)                 # words of exact quotient period d
def B_exact(d): return sum(mobius(d // e) * 2 ** ceil_half(e) for e in divisors(d) if (d // e) % 2) // 2  # GPT's B_d
def active_formula(n, s):
    g = math.gcd(n, s)
    return 2 ** (ceil_half(n) - 1) - (2 ** (ceil_half(g) - 1) if v2(s) >= v2(n) else 0)

# polyethylene: the § 166 notebook's Cinf_flory (check 6.1), with the bond-angle supplement th as a parameter
def Tm(th, ph):
    c, s, cp, sp_ = math.cos(th), math.sin(th), math.cos(ph), math.sin(ph)
    return np.array([[c, s, 0], [s * cp, -c * cp, sp_], [s * sp_, -c * sp_, -cp]])
PHIS = [0.0, 2 * math.pi / 3, -2 * math.pi / 3]
def Umat(sig, om): return np.array([[1, sig, sig], [1, sig, sig * om], [1, sig * om, sig]], float)
def Cinf_flory(sig, om, th=math.acos(1 / 3), n_list=(1600, 3200)):
    l = 1.0
    def Gm(ph):
        M = np.zeros((5, 5)); T_ = Tm(th, ph); M[0, 0] = 1; M[0, 1:4] = 2 * l * T_[0]; M[0, 4] = l * l
        M[1:4, 1:4] = T_; M[1:4, 4] = l * np.array([1, 0, 0]); M[4, 4] = 1; return M
    U = Umat(sig, om)
    BD = np.zeros((15, 15))
    for kk, p_ in enumerate(PHIS): BD[5 * kk:5 * kk + 5, 5 * kk:5 * kk + 5] = Gm(p_)
    Gs = np.kron(U, np.eye(5)) @ BD; out = []
    for n in n_list:
        v = np.kron(np.array([1., 0, 0]), np.array([1, 2 * l * math.cos(th), 2 * l * math.sin(th), 0, l * l]))
        last = np.kron(np.ones(3), np.array([l * l, l, 0, 0, 1])); zf = np.array([1., 0, 0])
        for _ in range(n - 2):
            v = v @ Gs; zf = zf @ U; sc = np.abs(zf).sum(); v /= sc; zf /= sc
        out.append((n, (v @ last) / zf.sum() / (n * l * l)))
    (n1, c1), (n2, c2) = out; return (c2 * n2 - c1 * n1) / (n2 - n1)
def Cinf_markov(sig, om, th=math.acos(1 / 3)):
    # independent route: the rotational states of an infinite chain are a stationary Markov chain;
    # C_inf = 1 + 2 sum_{m>=1} <T_1...T_m>_11 = 1 + 2 [a (I - calP)^-1 1]_11
    U = Umat(sig, om)
    w, vr = np.linalg.eig(U); i = int(np.argmax(w.real)); lam = w[i].real; r = np.abs(vr[:, i].real)
    w2, vl = np.linalg.eig(U.T); j = int(np.argmax(w2.real)); lft = np.abs(vl[:, j].real)
    Pm = U * r[None, :] / (lam * r[:, None]); pi = lft * r / (lft @ r)
    Ts = [Tm(th, ph) for ph in PHIS]
    calP = np.block([[Pm[a, b] * Ts[b] for b in range(3)] for a in range(3)])
    a = np.hstack([pi[k] * Ts[k] for k in range(3)]); one = np.vstack([np.eye(3)] * 3)
    return float(1 + 2 * (a @ np.linalg.solve(np.eye(9) - calP, one))[0, 0]), Pm, pi

# %% [markdown]
#Part 1 — the chords as operators (168.2).
#
#P = HJ, H and J commute, JHJ = H and J tau J = tau^-1. So (P tau^s)^2 = H J tau^s H J tau^s = H (J tau^s J)(J H J) tau^s = H tau^-s H tau^s. That map sends x to C^(p(x) xor p(tau^s x)) x, because p(Cx) = p(x). The masks add, and the sum telescopes: p(x) xor p(tau^s x) = q_0 xor q_1 xor ... xor q_(s-1). So **a chord of span s is the product of s consecutive keys**, Q^(s) = Q_0 Q_1 ... Q_(s-1). Since tau^n = C does not move a sheet pair, Q^(n) = I and spans repeat with period n.

# %%
ok = True
for n in range(2, 13):
    N2 = 2 * n; T = perm(tau, n); Pp = perm(P, n); Hp = perm(H, n); I = ident(n)
    Tp = [I]
    for s in range(1, N2): Tp.append(comp(T, Tp[-1]))
    ok &= comp(T, Tp[-1]) == I
    Q1 = comp(Pp, T, Pp, T)
    Qt = [comp(Tp[(-t) % N2], Q1, Tp[t]) for t in range(N2)]
    Qs = []
    for s in range(N2):
        q = comp(Pp, Tp[s], Pp, Tp[s]); Qs.append(q)
        ok &= q == comp(Hp, Tp[(-s) % N2], Hp, Tp[s])
        ok &= all(q[x] == (C(x, n) if pal(x, n) ^ pal(Tp[s][x], n) else x) for x in range(1 << n))
        prod = I
        for t in range(s): prod = comp(Qt[t], prod)
        ok &= q == prod
    ok &= all(Qt[t + n] == Qt[t] for t in range(n))
    ok &= all(comp(Qt[a], Qt[b]) == comp(Qt[b], Qt[a]) for a in range(n) for b in range(a + 1, n))
    ok &= all(comp(Qt[a], Qt[a]) == I for a in range(n))
    ok &= Qs[n] == I and all(Qs[s + n] == Qs[s] for s in range(n))
record('168.2', '(P tau^s)^2 = H tau^-s H tau^s, complementing x exactly when p([x]) xor p([tau^s x]) = 1; Q^(s) = Q_0...Q_(s-1); the Q_t commute and square to I; Q^(n) = I, Q^(s+n) = Q^(s)',
       'n = 2..12, s = 0..2n-1, every word', ok, 'every chord is a product of consecutive keys')

# %% [markdown]
#Part 2 — the orbits and their counts (168.3–168.4).
#
#- **Periods.** tau-bar^n = 1 on V_n, so a quotient period d divides n. If tau^d x = x, then tau^n x = x, but tau^n x = Cx. So tau^d x = Cx, and tau^n x = C^(n/d) x = Cx forces n/d odd.
#- **One palindrome per orbit** (Gemini's Theorem 1; this is GPT's proof). If x and tau^j x are both palindromes, then tau^j x = J tau^j x = tau^-j J x = tau^-j x. So tau^(2j) x = x, hence 2d | 2j and d | j: they are the same quotient point.
#- **Counting** (a proof of GPT's formula). A word with tau^d x = Cx is the antiperiodic extension s_(t+d) = NOT s_t of its first d bits, so there are 2^d of them. It is a palindrome exactly when its first block is one. Block m and its mirror block n/d - 1 - m carry complements of the same parity, because n/d - 1 is even, so the condition reduces to the first block. That gives 2^ceil(d/2) palindromes.
#- **Exact periods.** A word of exact period e satisfies tau^d x = Cx iff e | d and d/e is odd. Möbius inversion over those divisors gives the words of exact period d. Dividing by the 2d words of an orbit counts orbits, and dividing by the 2 palindromic words of a bearing orbit gives B_d.

# %%
ok3 = ok4 = True; ORB = {}; BEAR = {}; rows = []
for n in range(2, 21):
    orbs = quotient_orbits(n); per = Counter(); bear = Counter()
    for cyc in orbs:
        d = len(cyc); pc = [pal(x, n) for x in cyc]
        ok3 &= n % d == 0 and (n // d) % 2 == 1 and sum(pc) <= 1
        per[d] += 1
        if sum(pc): bear[d] += 1
        if n <= 16: ORB.setdefault(n, []).append((d, pc))
    for d in divisors(n):
        if (n // d) % 2: ok4 &= E_exact(d) % (2 * d) == 0 and per[d] == E_exact(d) // (2 * d) and bear[d] == B_exact(d)
        else: ok4 &= per[d] == 0
    ok4 &= len(orbs) == golomb(n) and sum(bear.values()) == 2 ** (ceil_half(n) - 1)
    BEAR[n] = bear; rows.append(f'{n}:{len(orbs)}/{sum(bear.values())}')
record('168.3', 'every quotient orbit has period d | n with n/d odd and at most one palindrome class', 'n = 2..20', ok3)
record('168.4', 'orbits of exact period d = (1/2d) sum mu(d/e) 2^e and B_d = (1/2) sum mu(d/e) 2^ceil(e/2) over e | d, d/e odd; totals A000016(n) and 2^(ceil(n/2)-1)',
       'n = 2..20', ok4, 'orbits/bearing ' + ' '.join(rows[-6:]))

# %% [markdown]
#Part 3 — where a chord acts (168.5–168.6).
#
#On a bearing orbit with its palindrome at j0, q_s(j) = p(j) xor p(j+s) equals 1 exactly at j = j0 and j = j0 - s. The one exception is d | s, when p(j) = p(j+s) everywhere. So **the chord of span s acts on the bearing orbits whose period does not divide s, and on each of them it flips exactly two sheet pairs**: the palindrome and the point s steps before it.
#
#**Closed form (new).** Suppose first that v2(s) < v2(n). Every admissible period d carries the full power of 2 in n (n/d is odd), so no d divides s, and the chord acts on all 2^(ceil(n/2)-1) bearing orbits. Otherwise, let g = gcd(n, s). The periods that divide s are exactly the d | g with g/d odd. Their bearing orbits hold the palindromes among the words with tau^g x = Cx, and there are 2^ceil(g/2) of those (Part 2, with g in place of d). So 2^(ceil(g/2)-1) orbits drop out.

# %%
ok5 = True; cnt5 = 0
for n in range(2, 17):
    for d, pc in ORB[n]:
        j0 = pc.index(1) if 1 in pc else None
        for s in range(1, 2 * n + 1):
            q = [pc[j] ^ pc[(j + s) % d] for j in range(d)]
            if j0 is not None and s % d: ok5 &= sum(q) == 2 and {j for j in range(d) if q[j]} == {j0, (j0 - s) % d}
            else: ok5 &= sum(q) == 0
            cnt5 += 1
record('168.5', 'the chord q_s has weight 2, at j0 and j0 - s, on a palindrome-bearing orbit whose period does not divide s, and weight 0 otherwise',
       'n = 2..16, every orbit, s = 1..2n', ok5, f'{cnt5} orbit-span pairs')
ok6 = True; tab = {}
for n in range(2, 21):
    for s in range(1, 2 * n + 1):
        act = sum(c for d, c in BEAR[n].items() if s % d)
        ok6 &= act == active_formula(n, s)
        if n in (12, 15, 16) and s <= n: tab.setdefault(n, []).append(act)
record('168.6', 'a chord of span s acts on 2^(ceil(n/2)-1) - [v2(s) >= v2(n)] 2^(ceil(g/2)-1) orbits, g = gcd(n, s)', 'n = 2..20, s = 1..2n', ok6,
       '; '.join(f'n={n}: s=1..{n} -> {tab[n]}' for n in (12, 15, 16)))

# %% [markdown]
#Part 4 — the spectrum of a chord (168.7).
#
#An active chord is two unit impulses, so q^_s(k) = p^(k) (1 + e^(2 pi i k s/d)), with p^(k) = e^(-2 pi i k j0/d) of modulus 1. The bracket vanishes only when e^(2 pi i k s/d) = -1. That needs 2ks = d (mod 2d), and hence an even d. **So at odd width no chord ever cancels a harmonic.** At even period, the half-span chord (s = d/2 mod d) is blind to every odd harmonic: two impulses half a period apart form a signal that the half-period shift leaves unchanged, and such a signal lives on the even harmonics. That is the Nyquist split of § 166 (state on the odd harmonics, the quadratic reader on the even ones), read on a quotient orbit.

# %%
ok7 = True; nz = nyq = 0
for n in range(2, 17):
    for d, pc in ORB[n]:
        if 1 not in pc: continue
        j0 = pc.index(1)
        for s in range(1, 2 * n + 1):
            if s % d == 0: continue
            q = [pc[j] ^ pc[(j + s) % d] for j in range(d)]
            zeros = []
            for k in range(d):
                qh = sum(q[j] * cmath.exp(-2j * math.pi * j * k / d) for j in range(d))
                ph = cmath.exp(-2j * math.pi * k * j0 / d)
                ok7 &= abs(qh - ph * (1 + cmath.exp(2j * math.pi * k * s / d))) < 1e-9 and abs(abs(ph) - 1) < 1e-12
                z = abs(qh) < 1e-9; zeros.append(z); nz += z
                ok7 &= z == (d % 2 == 0 and (k * s) % d == d // 2)
                if n % 2: ok7 &= not z
            if d % 2 == 0 and s % d == d // 2:
                nyq += 1; ok7 &= all(zeros[k] == (k % 2 == 1) for k in range(d))
record('168.7', "an active chord's DFT is p^(k)(1 + e^(2 pi i k s/d)); zeros only at even d, exactly where ks = d/2 (mod d); none at odd n; the half-span chord lives on the even harmonics",
       'n = 2..16, every active orbit and span', ok7, f'{nz} spectral zeros, all at even period; {nyq} half-span chords, each zero on every odd harmonic')

# %% [markdown]
#Part 5 — Gemini's keyboard (168.8).
#
#Right: (J tau)^2 = I, so tau and J alone close as a dihedral group of order 4n, and the only elements of it that fix every sheet pair are I and C. **Before C1 corrects J at the palindromes there is no local flip**; after it, K_n has one for every orbit pattern its masks can make. One word is off: Q = (P tau)^2 is the *dihedral defect*, not the commutator, since [P, tau] = P tau P tau^-1 = Q tau^-2. The count needs one correction too: the n translates Q_t have rank n - 1, because their masks sum to zero around every orbit, and the complement supplies the last independent flip. So K_n has rank n, except n - 1 at n = 4 (§ 167.5); Gemini's "K_n = (Z/2)^n" misses n = 4.

# %%
ok8a = all(comp(perm(J, n), perm(tau, n), perm(J, n), perm(tau, n)) == ident(n) for n in range(2, 13))
ok8b = True; orders = []
for n in range(3, 11):
    T, Jp = perm(tau, n), perm(J, n); e = tuple(ident(n)); Gset = {e}; frontier = [e]
    while frontier:
        new = []
        for g in frontier:
            for a in (T, Jp):
                h_ = tuple(a[i] for i in g)
                if h_ not in Gset: Gset.add(h_); new.append(h_)
        frontier = new
    fix = sorted(g for g in Gset if all(g[x] in (x, C(x, n)) for x in range(1 << n)))
    ok8b &= len(Gset) == 4 * n and fix == sorted([e, tuple(perm(C, n))]); orders.append(len(Gset))
ok8c = True
for n in range(2, 13):
    T, Ti, Pp = perm(tau, n), perm(tau_inv, n), perm(P, n)
    Q1 = comp(Pp, T, Pp, T); comm = comp(Pp, T, Pp, Ti)
    ok8c &= comm == comp(Q1, Ti, Ti) and comm != Q1
record('168.8', '(J tau)^2 = I; the only elements of <tau, J> fixing every sheet pair are I and C; [P, tau] = Q tau^-2, not Q',
       '(J tau)^2: n = 2..12; <tau, J>: n = 3..10; commutator: n = 2..12', ok8a and ok8b and ok8c, f'|<tau, J>| = {orders}')

# %% [markdown]
#Part 6 — Gemini's map, brute force and route (168.9–168.10).
#
#**Right.** d0 is a coboundary, so its circulation around the n-cycle is 0 for every word, and its image is exactly the even-weight vectors. H^1 of the cycle over F_2 is therefore one bit. D1, whose circulation is odd, is its nonzero class: the One Inverter as a cohomology class.
#
#**Not right.** The bit-reversed counter J inc J is conjugate to inc. From 0 its k-th state is J(k), so it reaches a target y at step J(y). Its steps-to-target are a permutation of 0..2^n - 1, with the same mean (2^n - 1)/2 and the same worst case 2^n - 1 as counting. Its first step flips the top bit, but that is just where its order starts, not a halving of the candidates.
#
#What halves the candidates at each step is a comparison with the target. That is Gemini's own "map" column, and it costs one query per bit. A constraint from the target's far end does the same work (§ 99.3's held end). A relabelling adds no information about the target, so it cannot shorten a search.

# %%
ok9 = True
for n in range(2, 17):
    img = set()
    for x in range(1 << n):
        b = [(x >> (n - 1 - k)) & 1 for k in range(n)]
        d0 = [b[k] ^ b[(k + 1) % n] for k in range(n)]; D1 = d0[:-1] + [d0[-1] ^ 1]
        ok9 &= sum(d0) % 2 == 0 and sum(D1) % 2 == 1
        img.add(int(''.join(map(str, d0)), 2))
    ok9 &= len(img) == 2 ** (n - 1) and all(bin(v).count('1') % 2 == 0 for v in img)
record('168.9', 'the circulation of d0 is 0 and of D1 is 1 for every word; im d0 = the 2^(n-1) even-weight vectors, so H^1(n-cycle; F2) is one bit and D1 its nonzero class',
       'n = 2..16, every word', ok9)
ok10 = True; means = []
for n in range(2, 17):
    N = 1 << n; step = [-1] * N; x = 0
    for k in range(N):
        if step[x] != -1: break
        step[x] = k; x = J(inc(J(x, n), n), n)
    ok10 &= x == 0 and min(step) == 0
    ok10 &= J(inc(J(0, n), n), n) == N >> 1
    ok10 &= all(step[y] == J(y, n) for y in range(N)) and sum(step) * 2 == N * (N - 1) and max(step) == N - 1
    means.append(sum(step) / N)
record('168.10', 'J inc J is one 2^n-cycle; its first step from 0 is 2^(n-1); it reaches y at step J(y): mean (2^n - 1)/2 and worst case 2^n - 1, as for inc',
       'n = 2..16, every target', ok10, f'mean steps at n = 16: {means[-1]:.1f} = (2^16 - 1)/2; a reordering, not a shortcut')

# %% [markdown]
#Part 7 — *Two Laps Home* v3: the bond-angle value (168.12; a reproduction, not a prediction).
#
#Section 8 of the paper says that opening the bond angle from the tetrahedral 109.47° to the 112° used in RIS treatments of polyethylene raises C_inf to 6.886 at the 413 K weights. This was first computed in the pre-publication check of 24 October, and the companion notebook did not reproduce it. Two methods follow, with the bond-angle supplement theta as the only change (theta = arccos(1/3) = 70.53° tetrahedral; theta = 68° for 112°).
#
#- **(a) Running product.** The § 166 notebook's generator-matrix running product (check 6.1).
#- **(b) Stationary sum.** The exact stationary sum C_inf = 1 + 2 [a (I - calP)^-1 1]_11 over the Markov chain of rotational states, where calP has blocks P(eta -> zeta) T(zeta) and a has blocks pi(eta) T(eta).
#
#**The outcome.** The two methods agree to better than 1e-7, and the 112° value is 6.8858. As sealed, 168.12 also said both give 6.229676 at the tetrahedral angle with the six-decimal weights. They give 6.229674. Table 3 and check 6.1 compute C_inf from the unrounded weights exp(-E/RT) but print the weights to six decimals, and the sixth decimal of C_inf moves with that rounding. This is logged as a sealed miss. 168.12b is the post-hoc check with the unrounded weights.

# %%
s413, o413 = 0.542507, 0.086621
th_tet, th_112 = math.acos(1 / 3), math.radians(180 - 112)
fa_tet, fa_112 = Cinf_flory(s413, o413, th_tet), Cinf_flory(s413, o413, th_112)
(fb_tet, Pm, pi_), (fb_112, _, _) = Cinf_markov(s413, o413, th_tet), Cinf_markov(s413, o413, th_112)
ind_a, ind_b = Cinf_flory(s413, 1.0), Cinf_markov(s413, 1.0)[0]
main12 = (round(fa_112, 4) == 6.8858 and round(fb_112, 4) == 6.8858 and abs(fa_112 - fb_112) < 1e-7 and abs(fa_tet - fb_tet) < 1e-7
          and abs(ind_a - 2 * (2 + s413) / (3 * s413)) < 1e-6 and abs(ind_b - 2 * (2 + s413) / (3 * s413)) < 1e-9 and np.allclose(Pm.sum(1), 1) and np.allclose(pi_ @ Pm, pi_))
tet12 = abs(fa_tet - 6.229676) < 5e-7 and abs(fb_tet - 6.229676) < 5e-7
if main12 and not tet12: MISS_WHY['168.12'] = f'the six-decimal weights give {fa_tet:.6f} at the tetrahedral angle; 6.229676 needs the unrounded weights'
record('168.12', 'C_inf at a 112° bond angle with the 413 K weights is 6.8858 by both methods; both give 6.229676 at the tetrahedral angle', 'sigma 0.542507, omega 0.086621, gauche +-120°',
       main12 and tet12, f'(a) {fa_tet:.6f} -> {fa_112:.6f}; (b) {fb_tet:.6f} -> {fb_112:.6f}; independent-rotation control (a) {ind_a:.6f}, (b) {ind_b:.6f} = 2(2+sigma)/(3 sigma)'
       + ('' if tet12 else f'; missed at the sixth decimal: the six-decimal weights give {fa_tet:.6f} at the tetrahedral angle'), miss=main12 and not tet12)
RGAS = 8.31446261815324
se, oe = math.exp(-2100 / (RGAS * 413)), math.exp(-8400 / (RGAS * 413))
ga_tet, ga_112 = Cinf_flory(se, oe, th_tet), Cinf_flory(se, oe, th_112)
gb_tet, gb_112 = Cinf_markov(se, oe, th_tet)[0], Cinf_markov(se, oe, th_112)[0]
s3, o3 = math.exp(-2100 / (RGAS * 300)), math.exp(-8400 / (RGAS * 300))
ok12b = (abs(ga_tet - 6.229676) < 5e-7 and abs(gb_tet - 6.229676) < 5e-7 and round(ga_112, 4) == 6.8858 and round(gb_112, 4) == 6.8858
         and abs(ga_112 - gb_112) < 1e-7 and round(se, 6) == s413 and round(oe, 6) == o413 and round(s3, 6) == 0.430888 and round(o3, 6) == 0.034471)
record('168.12b', 'post hoc, unsealed: with the unrounded weights exp(-E/RT) (E_g 2100, E_p 8400 J/mol) both methods give 6.229676 at the tetrahedral angle, as check 6.1 and Table 3 do, and 6.8858 at 112°; Table 3 prints the weights rounded to six decimals',
       'unrounded weights', ok12b, f'413 K: sigma {se:.9f}, omega {oe:.9f}; 300 K: sigma {s3:.9f}, omega {o3:.9f}; (a) {ga_tet:.6f} -> {ga_112:.6f}; (b) {gb_tet:.6f} -> {gb_112:.6f}')

# %%
npass = sum(1 for r in RESULTS if r[1]); fails = [r[0] for r in RESULTS if not r[1] and not r[5]]; misses = [r[0] for r in RESULTS if r[5]]
print()
print('NOT PASSED: ' + ', '.join(fails) if fails else (f'ALL CHECKS PASS ({npass} passed)' + ('; sealed miss logged: ' + '; '.join(f'{m} ({MISS_WHY.get(m, "see above")})' for m in misses) if misses else '')))
